name: POST /mcp/v1/call — registry-mcp stateless tool call
description:
Stateless tool-call surface for the local MCP proxy (FR-MCP-L4) and the cloud-builder /api/build/* routes. Returns the same ToolResult shape the SSE transport would produce, so a caller can treat both transports identically. Takes {name, arguments}; name is required and arguments defaults to {}. Dispatch forks on the tool name: a name in WRITE_TOOL_NAMES goes to dispatchWriteTool with the resolved TenantContext, everything else to the read-only dispatchTool, which is why a write tool called without a tenant-bearing credential fails inside the dispatcher rather than at the door. NOTE THE STATUS SEMANTICS: a tool that fails answers 200 with a ToolResult carrying isError:true, NOT a 4xx - the HTTP status describes the transport, the body describes the tool, and a caller that only checks the status will read every tool failure as success. Authn is Bearer OR x-projex-api-key via extractTenantContext, and a per-tenant rate limiter answers 429 before dispatch.

WHY testability IS manual: this route is served by the STANDALONE registry-mcp service, not by the api-gateway. It is a separate compose service on its own origin and port, and the api-gateway does not mount or proxy it - `grep registry-mcp services/api-gateway/src/app.ts` returns nothing. The api test suite drives one base URL (the gateway, :4000 locally), so dispatching this path there is a guaranteed 404 against Fastify's not-found handler and would assert nothing about registry-mcp. It also does not run in the local compose stack. To exercise it, point a client at the registry-mcp service directly with a valid tenant credential. This is a DIFFERENT-ORIGIN limitation, not a missing-payload or uncaptured-path-param one - it is not the case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.

errorCases.when: extractTenantContext rejects the credential — no Bearer and no x-projex-api-key, an unverifiable token, or an api key the resolver cannot resolve. The thrown AuthError supplies its own statusCode, so the exact status follows that error rather than being fixed here
The body is absent, not an object, or carries no name — checked after authn and rate limiting, so an unauthenticated caller sees 401 rather than this
The per-tenant limiter refuses the call, keyed on tenant_id and falling back to sub when the credential carries no tenant
The request reached the api-gateway rather than the registry-mcp service — the gateway does not mount this route, which is exactly why this definition is testability:manual

_originNote: Served by services/registry-mcp (its own compose service and port), NOT the api-gateway the suite targets. An unhandled tool dispatch failure surfaces as 200 with isError:true in the ToolResult body, so status alone never distinguishes a tool error from success.
